title: Documentation Home
description: What VELLUM is, how its two PostgreSQL data planes fit together, and where to begin.
text: VELLUM Documentation VELLUM is a multi-tenant document database built entirely on PostgreSQL/JSONB. You get hierarchical collections, typed JSON documents, structured queries with cursor pagination, atomic field transforms, optimistic-concurrency transactions, and realtime WebSocket streams — through a small TypeScript SDK ( @vellumdb/sdk-js ) or plain HTTP. There is one stateful runtime dependency: PostgreSQL . No Redis, no message broker, and no separate cache service. Realtime is built on PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY plus a durable outbox; caching and rate limits use short-lived in-process state with PostgreSQL backing where durability matters; transactions are native PostgreSQL transactions. :::note VELLUM's public document API is scoped by API key with an optional EdDSA end-user bearer. End-user credentials are fully isolated from every other surface and share only crypto primitives — see [End-User Authentication](./end-user-auth.md). ::: Scenario Imagine you are building a multi-tenant task manager. Each customer (tenant) gets its own project with one project, and you need to store tasks, query the open ones, react to changes live, and keep a strict audit trail — all without ope

text: Public Data Plane REST API The public document plane is implemented directly in apps/api/src/app.ts . It is the only surface that reads/writes customer documents. Every operation is scoped by (projectId) from the URL and authenticated by an API key. Business logic (validation, rules evaluation, SQL) lives in @vellum/query-engine , @vellum/document-engine , and @vellum/storage — never in the route handlers. Tenant scoping and authentication Every route in this section has the shape: Requirement Detail :--- :--- :projectId Project UUID. Resolved via controlStore.getProject . API key Mandatory. When present it must be a valid signed JWT ( verifyEndUserJwtSync ); otherwise 401 . Its claims become the authContext used by security rules. Project state suspended → 403 PERMISSION_DENIED ; throttled → 429 RATE_LIMITED . title: Authentication
description: API keys, end-user tokens, key rotation, and least-privilege access.
text: Authentication VELLUM credentials are fully isolated per surface. They share only stateless crypto primitives; storage, signing secrets, JWT typ / iss / aud , claims and middleware are fully separate, so a token minted for one surface is rejected anywhere else. The document plane ( /v1/projects/... ) uses API keys via x-vellum-api-key (legacy x-project-key ), with an optional EdDSA-only end-user bearer. There is no HS256 fallback, anonymous fallback or implicit master key. See [End-User Authentication](./end-user-auth.md) for tokens, refresh rotation, the full REST reference and rate limits. :::note A public API key can safely appear in a browser or mobile app, but it grants zero implicit data access . Every operation is evaluated against the project's active security ruleset. A server key bypasses rules only for the explicit scopes it carries. ::: Scenario You are adding a feature where users sign in to your app and the client reads only its own documents. You issue a public pk_ key for the browser, attach the signed-in user's JWT on each request, and rely on security rules to enforce ownership — keeping the master sk_ key on your server only. title: CRUD & Document Paths
description: Canonical paths, document and collection references, create/set/update/delete, ifVersion, and the tagged wire format.
text: CRUD & Document Paths Every resource in the data plane is addressed by a canonical, / -separated UTF-8 path. Paths alternate between collection segments and document-id segments. Scenario You are modeling a customer with their orders: one document at users/u_123 , plus a subcollection of orders at users/u_123/orders/ord_456 . You create the user, patch a field with a server timestamp, guard the update with a version precondition, and then read the document with its metadata. Path rules Kind Segments Examples :--- :--- :--- Document Even, 2–10 users/u_123 , users/u_123/orders/ord_456 Collection Odd, 1–9 users , users/u_123/orders A path of depth 10 allows five nested collections. For users/u_123/orders/ord_456 : Component Value :--- :--- path users/u_123/orders/ord_456 collectionPath users/u_123/orders collectionGroup orders documentId ord_456 pathDepth 4 Segment constraints - At most 1,500 bytes per segment (UTF-8). - No / , NUL byte, or ASCII control characters ( 0x00 – 0x1F ). - . and .. are rejected. - Segments matching ^__. __$ (for example __name__ ) are reserved for engine metadata and rejected on user paths. :::warning Exceeding the depth limit raises INVALID_DOCUMENT_PATH

title: End-User Authentication
description: EdDSA-only end-user tokens, refresh rotation with a 15 s grace window, profile projection, REST surfaces, WS auth and rate limits.
text: End-User Authentication Project end-user tokens are fully isolated from every other credential. The token layer shares only stateless crypto primitives from @vellum/auth (scrypt, AES-256-GCM, SHA-256, TOTP, token generators, rotation math) with other surfaces; storage, signing keys, JWT typ / iss / aud , claims, session services and middleware are 100% separate, so a token from another surface is always rejected here. Surface Sessions Secret Algorithm typ iss aud :--- :--- :--- :--- :--- :--- :--- project end users data_db.project_auth_ (FORCE RLS) project Ed25519 key EdDSA vellum+enduser+jwt https://api.vellum.dev/v1/projects/<projectId /auth <projectId :::important No HS256 fallback End-user tokens are verified EdDSA-only on both HTTP and WebSocket, against the project's Ed25519 public key. Any HS256 token is rejected on the document plane even with a valid project API key. ::: End-user tokens and JWKS Access tokens carry iss , sub , aud=projectId , email , email_verified , is_anonymous , claims , iat , exp , auth_time and jti , signed per project. title: Tagged Wire Format & Path Grammar
description: Canonical $t/$v tagged types, $op field transforms, path grammar and the locked v1 size/depth limits.
text: Tagged Wire Format & Path Grammar Source of truth: packages/core/src/{wire-format,paths,limits,sort-key}.ts , packages/api-contract/src/schemas/documents.ts , and docs/02-wire-format-and-paths.md . This is the authoritative compact reference; for design rationale see [Canonical Paths & Tagged Wire Format](../../02-wire-format-and-paths.md). Why tags JSON has no native int64, timestamp, byte, reference or geopoint type. VELLUM uses a reserved wrapper {"$t": "<tag ", "$v": <value } so extended types never collide with user maps. Primitives ( null , boolean, string, finite number, array, plain map) are stored untagged so PostgreSQL jsonb GIN indexes can address them directly. TypeScript constructors live in WireValue ( @vellum/core ); the Dart SDK exposes VellumWire . title: Field Transforms
description: All atomic fieldOp sentinels, how they are applied, their ordering, and restrictions.
text: Field Transforms Field transforms let the server compute a field value atomically, avoiding a read-modify-write race. The SDK exposes five helpers under fieldOp ; on the wire each becomes a sentinel object with a $op key. Scenario Several users can "like" a post at the same time, and you want an accurate likeCount without coordinating clients. You use increment(1) to bump the counter atomically and arrayUnion to record unique reactor ids — the server applies both in one transaction, so no update is lost. The five operations SDK helper Wire sentinel Behavior :--- :--- :--- fieldOp.serverTimestamp() { "$op": "serverTimestamp" } Replaced with the transaction's UTC timestamp as { "$t": "ts", "$v": "...", "$ms": ... } . fieldOp.increment(n = 1) { "$op": "inc", "by": n } Adds n to the current value. Missing field initializes to n . fieldOp.arrayUnion(...items) { "$op": "arrayUnion", "elements": [...] } Appends items not already present (typed deep equality). fieldOp.arrayRemove(...items) { "$op": "arrayRemove", "elements": [...] } Removes every occurrence matching any item. fieldOp.deleteField() { "$op": "deleteField" } Removes the field from its parent map. arrayUnion and arrayRemove a

title: Pagination
description: HMAC-signed opaque cursors, startAfter vs startAt, bounded-memory streaming with pages()/stream() in JS and streamPages()/streamDocuments() in Flutter.
text: Pagination VELLUM uses keyset cursor pagination backed by HMAC-signed opaque cursors and a deterministic document_id tie-breaker. SQL OFFSET is never used, so deep pages stay O(log N) and never skip or duplicate rows under concurrent inserts. --- Manual Cursor Pagination ( startAfter / startAt ) Every QuerySnapshot returns nextCursor: string null . Pass it to startAfter(cursor) for the next exclusive page (or startAt(cursor) in @vellumdb/sdk-js for an inclusive boundary): TypeScript ( @vellumdb/sdk-js ) Flutter / Dart ( vellum_flutter ) --- Enterprise Bounded-Memory Streaming For ETL pipelines, exports, backfills, or infinite scroll feeds, prefer the built-in streaming iterators instead of hand-rolled cursor loops. Both SDKs guard against empty pages and stuck cursors automatically. title: Composite Indexes
description: Tenant composite indexes as rows, order-preserving sort keys, creation and status, when an index is needed, and duplicate conflicts.
text: Composite Indexes Composite indexes accelerate queries that filter or sort on custom document fields. In a multi-tenant service, running CREATE INDEX per customer on the shared documents table would cause catalog bloat and DDL locks. VELLUM therefore stores indexes as rows , never as customer DDL. Scenario Your reporting screen filters users by status and sorts by priority desc , and the query starts failing with FAILED_PRECONDITION and a suggestedIndex . You register that index with a server key, poll until its status is ready , and then the query runs as a single B-tree range scan. How tenant indexes work Table Role :--- :--- document_indexes Index definition: collection path, ordered field list, definition hash, build status. document_index_entries One row per document in the index, keyed by an order-preserving sort_key BYTEA . An index definition names up to 3 fields , each with a path and a direction: The sort key encodes each field value with a type-prefix byte (missing, null, boolean, numeric, string, timestamp, reference, bytes), then escapes delimiters so the key preserves the natural ordering of the logical values. If a concurrent writer modifies a read document, the server responds with ABORTED_CONFLICT ( 409 ) and the SDK automatically retries with jittered backoff up to maxAttempts (default 5 ). title: Security Rules
description: The v1 JSON rules AST, deterministic deny-by-default evaluation, validation bounds, publishing, and simulation.
text: Security Rules Security rules decide whether a public API key ( pk_ ) may read or write a document. They are stored as a versioned JSON Abstract Syntax Tree in the control plane and evaluated synchronously in memory — never by generating or executing code. :::note Server keys ( sk_ ) bypass the rules AST for operations covered by their scopes. Public keys always evaluate rules; with no active ruleset, access is denied. ::: Scenario You run a multi-user app where each user may read and write only their own users/{userId} document, while a small admin group may read all users. You publish a ruleset that binds ownership to the path wildcard, check it in the Rule Simulator, and verify that an unauthorized pk_ request gets PERMISSION_DENIED . Ruleset shape (v1) version must be 1 and rules must be an array. Each rule has a match path pattern and an allow object whose keys are operations: get , list , create , update , delete , plus the shorthands read (covers get / list ) and write (covers create / update / delete ). title: Errors & Limits
description: Canonical error codes with HTTP statuses, and the locked v1 quotas enforced by @vellum/core.
text: Errors & Limits All failures use one canonical envelope and one set of error codes, defined in @vellum/core ( SYSTEM_LIMITS and VellumError ). Every HTTP response also carries an X-Request-Id header. Scenario You are wiring up client-side error handling and want retries only for transient failures: a version conflict should re-read and retry, a rate limit should back off using Retry-After , while a permissions error should surface to the user. You branch on the canonical code from the error envelope. Error envelope In the SDK, failed requests throw an Error with code , status , details , and requestId copied from the envelope. The details object is typed as a record and its keys vary by code; do not rely on a fixed shape. Canonical error codes Code HTTP Typical cause :--- :--- :--- INVALID_ARGUMENT 400 Malformed request, disallowed sentinel, bad config value. INVALID_DOCUMENT_PATH 400 Bad path depth, over-long or reserved segment. INVALID_FIELD_NAME 400 Empty, over-long, control-character, or prototype-pollution field name. title: Production Checklist
description: Hardening checklist for deploying VELLUM with @vellumdb/sdk-js and vellum_flutter — keys, auth storage, timeouts, retries, caching, streaming, realtime, and lifecycle disposal.
text: Production Checklist Verify every item below before shipping a VELLUM-backed application to production. --- 1. API Keys, Security Rules & Input Hygiene - [ ] Key separation : Use publishable keys ( pk_... ) in browser and Flutter clients; keep secret keys ( sk_... ) strictly on trusted backend servers. - [ ] Default-deny Security Rules : Ensure every user-accessible collection enforces auth.uid ownership or role claims rather than relying on client filtering. - [ ] No raw credentials in logs : vellum_flutter automatically redacts pk_ / sk_ , Bearer , and JWTs in toString() , and @vellumdb/sdk-js never logs tokens or exposes them in db.auth.toJSON() . title: Deployment & Hosting
description: Primary two-project Vercel path, the repository deployment pause, and optional self-hosting adapters.
text: Deployment & Hosting Primary path The repository's primary path is two independent Vercel projects: the API rooted at apps/api , and the static web frontend rooted at the repository root, which serves the web application at / and the documentation at /docs/ . It calls the separate API origin configured by VITE_API_BASE_URL ; the API allows the exact frontend origin in CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS . Automatic Git deployments are paused in both vercel.json files, including production/main. Build and test CI still runs. Merging a PR does not deploy. Do not re-enable automation or issue a manual deployment as part of routine code cleanup. From the repository checkout, start at docs/deployment/README.md . The full settings table, CORS rules, checks and rollback procedure live in docs/DEPLOYMENT-SPLIT.md . corepack pnpm deploy:plan prints an environment-name audit and plan only; it does not deploy or change account settings. Local development is different The local gateway at http://localhost:3000 serves the web frontend and proxies /v1 HTTP/WebSocket requests to the API at http://localhost:8080 . This same-origin proxy is a development convenience, not the primary Vercel production topology. F
